amendments.rule: Where the ASV converts a Greek circumstantial participle into a coordinate clause, the supplied English juncture *and* is a rule 7 helper on the verb of the clause it **introduces**, never on the participle it follows, and never `added`. `ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν` → *cast them down to hell, and committed them* gives *and committed* to the finite verb, as `φθεγξάμενον … ἐκώλυσεν` → *spake with man's voice and stayed* gives *and stayed* to `ἐκώλυσεν` and leaves `φθεγξάμενον` a bare *spake*. Rule 29 is what the corpus cites for this, by name, at 1PE.3.19, EPH.2.17, 1PE.1.13, JHN.9.11 and JHN.21.12, and the principle carries unchanged from a compound numeral to a clause: an obligatory English juncture is a helper on what it introduces. The corpus places such a juncture on the verb it introduces in thirty-four units across twenty-one chapters — JHN.8.2, JHN.8.6, JHN.8.7, JHN.8.8, JHN.2.15, JHN.12.3, JHN.13.4, JHN.19.2, EPH.2.17, 1PE.3.19 and 1PE.1.13 among them — against REV.1.1 `ἀποστείλας` → *sent and* alone on the participle it follows. The coordinate clause need not be **finite**: the word *finite* names the ordinary case and is not a scope, what licenses the fold being that a participle standing in the coordination has had its subordination converted into coordination. So where the ASV renders such a participle as one bare complement of a governing verb and coordinates it with a second complement, the juncture is still a rule 7 helper on the verb of the clause it introduces, whatever that clause's English finiteness: `Θέλεις εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀναβὰς ἐκεῖ κριθῆναι` → *Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem and there be judged* gives the discontinuous *and … be judged* to `κριθῆναι` under rule 15, an adverb of the introduced clause standing between, and leaves `ἀναβάς` a bare *go up*. Rule 86 is not the contrast and must not be read as making such a word `added`: its test is whether a source token licenses the word, and a participle standing in the same clause is exactly such a token, which is why no corpus unit has ever marked a participle-to-finite conversion juncture `added`. Rule 98 is the near contrast and its own scope is what keeps the two apart: it reaches an asyndetic seam between two **like** constituents each rendered in its own class — two infinitives, two attributive participles, two adjectives — where nothing has been converted and only the coordination is supplied, and a participle coordinated with a constituent of another class is not that seam. So ask whether a participle stands in the coordination before asking how finite the English is, and never decide it from the English alone. The four `added` units whose English is a bare *and* are all something else — 2CO.13.14 twice, where the Greek stands in the previous verse under rule 37; JHN.9.28, whose connective its unit's excluded fallback dropped under rule 97; and REV.15.6, a juncture between adjectives. An expressed Greek conjunction is untouched by this and is aligned in the ordinary way.
amendments.why: ACT.25 split on this: 25.5 folded a supplied *and* onto the verb of the clause it introduced, while 25.9 marked the structurally identical juncture `added`. The cause is the word *finite* in rule 88's opening — at 25.9 the ASV renders both coordinated clauses as bare complements of *Wilt thou*, so rule 88's literal terms did not reach the case and rule 98's like-constituent scope did not either, leaving a gap between them. The amendment widens *finite* to *coordinate*, states the operative test (a participle standing in the coordination, which is rule 86's licensing token), and marks the boundary against rule 98 from rule 98's own wording. It contradicts nothing: rule 88's thirty-four-to-one line stands, and every `added` unit rule 98 names is a like-constituent seam. Rule 98's later qualification of rule 88's closing aside is preserved verbatim, so its cross-reference still lands.

conventions: A supplied English juncture (*and*, *but*) coordinating a converted circumstantial participle with the clause beside it is folded onto the verb of the clause it introduces under rule 88 throughout this chapter — 25.5, 25.6 twice, 25.9, 25.13 and 25.17 twice — and is never `added`, whether or not the ASV renders the coordinated clauses finitely. Rule 98's `added` seam is not reached anywhere in ACT.25: no two coordinated constituents here are of the same class and each rendered in its own.

μὲν οὖν stands twice with a single English word written for the pair, and the word decides which particle keeps it under rule 70, the other standing `unrepresented`. 25.4 gives the adversative *Howbeit* to μέν; 25.11 gives *then* to οὖν. This is rule 24's habit and not two analyses, and each unit's note names the competing reading.

The article of a temporal dative phrase is decided by whether the ASV's noun glosses the adverb's lexeme. τῇ ἐπαύριον → *on the morrow* (25.6, 25.23) leaves *morrow* on the adverb and gives the article only *on the*; τῇ ἑξῆς → *on the next day* (25.17) gives the supplied nominal *day* to the article under rules 22 and 102, headed there, and leaves *next* bare on the adverb. Rule 66's test — whether the English noun glosses an element of the lexeme — is what separates them.

*the principal men* is written twice from different Greek and is analysed twice accordingly. At 25.2 οἱ πρῶτοι has no expressed noun, so the article takes *the … men* under rule 102 and πρῶτοι keeps a bare *principal*. At 25.23 ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατ' ἐξοχήν expresses the noun in front of its article, so under rule 31 ἀνδράσιν keeps *the … men*, τοῖς is `unrepresented` (no relative clause being written for it), and κατ' ἐξοχήν takes *principal* as one unit under rules 94 and 39.

report: One genuine cross-verse split, invisible to the lemma table because it turns on an `added` unit: the supplied juncture *and*. ACT.25.5 folds it onto the verb it introduces under rule 88 (a converted circumstantial participle coordinated with the clause beside it); ACT.25.9 marks the same construction `added` under rule 98. ACT.25.9 is patched to match, the juncture going to κριθῆναι discontinuously under rule 15.

Rule 98's scope is an asyndetic seam between two like constituents each rendered in its own class; ACT.25.9 coordinates a participle with an infinitive, which is rule 88's case and rule 86's licensing token. What let the two verses come apart is the word *finite* in rule 88's opening: in 25.9 the ASV renders both clauses as bare complements of *Wilt thou*, so neither rule's literal terms reached the case. That is the amendment returned.

Checked and rejected as non-splits, each licensed by the source or by the ASV's own wording: τῇ ἐπαύριον (25.6, 25.23) against τῇ ἑξῆς (25.17), separated by rule 102's supplied-nominal test; οἱ πρῶτοι (25.2) against ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατ' ἐξοχήν (25.23), separated by whether a head noun is expressed; μὲν οὖν at 25.4 and 25.11, which rule 70 decides by the word written and expressly permits to differ; τε aligned at 25.2, 25.16 and 25.24 and empty at 25.23, decided by the count of English conjunctions; ἐπικαλέω and αἰτέω particles kept inside the verb at 25.11, 25.12, 25.15 and 25.25 under rule 106's accusative arm, against the expressed ἐπί at 25.12 taking its own word.

The two remaining `added` units are correct and stay. ACT.25.4 *thither* resumes εἰς Καισάρειαν, whose English is spent, and ἐκπορεύεσθαι's English is complete without it, so rule 103's licensing test makes it added; ACT.25.7's supplied *him* and ACT.25.25's are the contrast, each completing a verb whose English is incomplete. ACT.25.11 *true* is a lexical predicate adjective, which rule 7's list does not reach.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error, and no accepted edge was changed to improve the rate. All eight are contract-mandated conventions — article before a name (25.8, 25.14) under rule 23; article displaced by a possessive (25.10 *Caesar's*, 25.19 *their own*) under rules 20 and 47; μὲν οὖν (25.4, 25.11) under rule 70; κατά compressed into the possessive *Paul's case* (25.14) under rule 36; and a καί whose clause the ASV recast as a prepositional phrase (25.23) under rule 23.
Four conventions recorded against 41 repeated notes and none previously logged; the rest of the repetitions restate contract rules and are left unlogged.
